title: SYN-DIGITS: A Synthetic Control Framework for Calibrated Digital Twin Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2604.07513v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Persona simulation based on large language models---often referred to as digital twin simulation---is increasingly used for market research, recommender systems, and social science research. However, these simulations often exhibit systematic bias and miscalibration relative to real human behavior. We propose SYN-DIGITS, a model-agnostic, post-hoc calibration framework that learns relationships among questions from digital twins and transfers them to predict human responses. We focus on a cold-start setting in which no human response to the target question is observed, so calibration must rely on digital twins and human data on reference questions. Our analysis shows that, though digital twins may not reproduce individual human responses accurately, they can capture nontrivial relationships among questions that can be effectively transferred to the human side. translated_title: SYN-DIGITS：用于校准数字孪生模拟的合成控制框架
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型的角色模拟（通常称为数字孪生模拟）正越来越多地被应用于市场研究、推荐系统和社会科学研究。然而，这些模拟相对于真实人类行为往往存在系统性偏差和校准失准问题。我们提出了SYN-DIGITS，一个模型无关的事后校准框架，它从数字孪生中学习问题之间的关系，并将其迁移用于预测人类回答。我们聚焦于一个冷启动场景：即没有观察到人类对目标问题的回答，因此校准必须依赖数字孪生数据以及人类在参考问题上的数据。我们的分析表明，尽管数字孪生可能无法准确复现个体的人类回答，但它们能够捕捉问题之间非平凡的关系，这些关系可以有效地迁移到人类一侧。当个体层面的数据不可用且我们只能获取……
tldr: 提出SYN-DIGITS框架，一种模型无关的事后校准方法，通过从数字孪生中学习问题间的关系并迁移到人类侧，在无目标问题人类回答数据的冷启动场景下有效校准大语言模型角色模拟的偏差。
en_tdlr: SYN-DIGITS is a model-agnostic post-hoc calibration framework that learns relationships among questions from digital twins and transfers them to predict human responses, enabling calibrated LLM persona simulation in cold-start settings where no human data on the target question is available.
